1: Strict target-label-free computational workflow. Source-only scaling precedes transductive adaptation of the whole unlabeled target block. Candidate runs use the fixed 11-value μ grid and 10 outputs. Label-free selection or voting is frozen and hashed before retrospective target evaluation. Target labels enter only the terminal evaluation block; oracle selection and target-support attribution are retrospective and have no feedback path.
2: UCI primary same-label-support target batches B2 and B6–B10 (6 domains; 66 saved candidate runs). Target-present macro-F1 is plotted for each fixed μ value from 0 to 1 in increments of 0.1. Lines join saved metrics without fitting or aggregation. Both benchmark figures use identical 0–1 axes. These target-label-based curves and their maxima are retrospective evaluation, not deployable tuning.
3: External chronological domains T1–T7 (7 domains; 77 saved candidate runs) from the reconstructed 700-row derived benchmark; the distributed feature table contains 624 rows. Target-present macro-F1 is plotted for each fixed μ value from 0 to 1 in increments of 0.1. Lines join saved metrics without fitting or aggregation. Both benchmark figures use identical 0–1 axes. These target-label-based curves and their maxima are retrospective evaluation, not deployable tuning.
5: Per-domain oracle gaps for six deployable strategies, shown separately for UCI primary same-label-support (6 domains) and external primary (7 domains). Gap equals the retrospective best single-μ Target-present Macro-F1 minus strategy macro-F1; zero is parity and negative values favor voting over the single-μ oracle. Distinct marker shapes and colors identify target domains; the same shape key remains readable in grayscale. Horizontal offsets separate points. The 0.15 line is a pre-fixed descriptive catastrophic-gap threshold, not a statistical test. Hard-onehot EnsV is an applicability baseline. No pooling across datasets or significance inference is used.
6: Present-class pseudo-label support collapse in comparable output states 1–10. Each left cell counts output states with at least one retrospectively true-present class missing from pseudo-label support (0–10 states) for a target domain and fixed μ. UCI primary has 33/66 affected runs and 156/660 affected states; external has 0/77 and 0/770. Separate right cells count affected bootstrap-state-0 runs across 11 μ values per domain (UCI 55/66; external 0/77). Output panels share a 0–10 color scale; bootstrap panels use a separate 0–11 scale because their unit is candidate runs rather than output states. Every cell prints its exact count, so color is redundant. Repeated states and μ runs are not independent trials. True-present support is retrospectively frozen metadata, not a fitting input; absent true classes are excluded. Zero observed external collapse does not establish its absence in other settings.
S1: Supplementary Figure S1 (former Figure 4). Per-domain range (maximum minus minimum; left) and population standard deviation (right) of Target-present Macro-F1 across the fixed 11-value μ grid. Each labeled point is one target domain: UCI primary B2/B6–B10 (6 domains) or external T1–T7 (7 domains). Both panels use the same full 0–1 vertical scale in absolute F1 units; horizontal offsets separate domain points. All values are frozen D016 descriptive summaries; there are no pooled averages, inferential tests, or fitted trends. The external task is the reconstructed 700-row derived benchmark, distinct from the distributed 624-row feature table.
